glosses: To keep (something, such as an aircraft) in a stationary state in the air.
Of a bird: to shelter (chicks) under its body and wings; (by extension) of a thing: to cover or surround (something).

examples.text: Castration has a ſtrange effect: it emaſculates both man, beaſt, and bird, and brings them to a near reſemblance of the other ſex. […] Capons have ſmall combs and gills, and look pallid about the head, like pullets; they alſo vvalk vvithout any parade, and hover chickens like hens.

glosses: Of a bird or insect: to flap (its wings) so it can remain stationary in the air.

examples.text: O'er the deer Corps ſomtimes her vvings ſhe [an eagle] hovers, / Somtimes the dead breſt vvith her breſt ſhe covers, […]

examples.text: The hummingbird hovered by the plant.

glosses: To remain persistently in one's thoughts.

examples.text: Exploring, I found another short gallery running transversely to the first. glosses: To prevent from reaching a decision, especially by refusing to join in a verdict that must be unanimous.

examples.text: One obstinate juror can hang a jury.

glosses: To stop responding to manual input devices such as the keyboard and mouse.

examples.text: The computer has hung again. Not even pressing <Ctrl>+<Alt>+<Del> works.

glosses: To cause (a program or computer) to stop responding.

examples.text: The program has a bug that can hang the system.

glosses: To cause (a piece) to become vulnerable to capture.

examples.text: If you move there, you'll hang your rook.

glosses: To be vulnerable to capture.
